doc:
# CTheorem — Renormalization

Unformalized claims gathered verbatim from [wiphy.org](https://wiphy.org/) (query: “holographic c-theorem”).

claims.name: theorem_suggests_deep_connection_between
claims.statement: The theorem suggests a deep connection between the holographic Zamolodchikov-Polchinski theorem and the holographic $c$-theorem.

sources.title: Higher derivative corrections in holographic Zamolodchikov-Polchinski theorem

claims.name: holographic_theorem_related_twodimensional_fieldtheory
claims.statement: The holographic C theorem is related to the two-dimensional field-theory C theorem that relies on the Zamolodchikov metric.

sources.title: A Field-theoretical Interpretation of the Holographic Renormalization Group

claims.name: theorem_equivalent_theorem_theories_satisfying
claims.statement: An $F$-theorem is equivalent to a $C_T$-theorem for theories satisfying the holographic relation.

sources.title: Precision test of AdS$_6$/CFT$_5$ in Type IIB

claims.name: boundary_central_charges_satisfy_holographic
claims.statement: The boundary central charges satisfy a holographic $c$-like theorem.

sources.title: A New Proposal for Holographic BCFT

claims.name: constructed_models_consistent_holographic_ctheorem
claims.statement: The constructed models are consistent with a holographic c-theorem.

sources.title: Extended massive gravity in three dimensions

claims.name: consistent_results_require_application_holographic
claims.statement: Consistent results require the application of the holographic c-theorem.

sources.title: Holographic Entanglement Entropy for d=4 N=2 SCFTs in F-theory

claims.name: holographic_ctheorem_evaluated_twodimensional_gravity
claims.statement: The holographic c-theorem is evaluated in two-dimensional gravity.

sources.title: Holographic renormalization group flows in two-dimensional gravity and $AdS$ black holes

claims.name: holographic_theorem_does_not_apply
claims.statement: The holographic $c$-theorem does not apply to these solutions.

sources.title: Gravity duals of cyclic RG flows, with strings attached

claims.name: abstract_addresses_ctheorem_setting_via
claims.statement: The abstract addresses the C-theorem setting via holographic duality.

claims.name: holographic_function_monotonically_decreasing_along
claims.statement: The holographic $c$-function $a_d(r)$ is monotonically decreasing along the renormalization group flow, giving a holographic $c$-theorem.

claims.name: quasitopological_gravity_naturally_gives_rise
claims.statement: Quasi-topological gravity naturally gives rise to a holographic c-theorem.

claims.name: obtained_boundary_central_charges_satisfy
claims.statement: The obtained boundary central charges satisfy a holographic c-like theorem.

sources.title: On New Proposal for Holographic BCFT

claims.name: cone_holography_neumann_boundary_conditions
claims.statement: Cone holography with Neumann boundary conditions obeys the holographic $c$-theorem.

sources.title: Cone Holography with Neumann Boundary Conditions and Brane-localized Gauge Fields

claims.name: holographic_limit_extends_more_general
claims.statement: The holographic limit extends to more general higher-dimensional theories whenever a holographic $c$-theorem holds.

sources.title: Three Dimensional Modified Gravities as Holographic Limits of Lancsoz-Lovelock Theories

claims.name: some_unphysical_models_nonunitary_operators
claims.statement: Some 'unphysical' models with nonunitary operators still satisfy a holographic c-theorem.

claims.name: angularmomentum_invariance_provides_another_realization
claims.statement: The angular-momentum invariance provides another realization of the holographic c-theorem.

sources.title: Conserved quantities and Virasoro algebra in New massive gravity

claims.name: holographic_function_runs_accordance_theorem
claims.statement: The holographic $c$ function runs in accordance with the $c$-theorem as the boundary universe evolves.

claims.name: unitarity_constraints_more_than_sufficient
claims.statement: The unitarity constraints are more than sufficient to produce a holographic c-theorem.
